narrative.overview:
Hugin is a map sheet, not a dashboard. The page is warm-grey paper with ink on it, and the only colours are the map's own: contour brown, forest, lake and rust, each with one job. Structure comes from hairlines and alignment, the way a printed sheet separates its parts, never from boxed panels or tiles. Time is the main axis: every open ad is drawn as a lifeline from the day it appeared to its frist, under one alternating week scale bar, with a solid today line and a dashed seen mark the user moves.

Density is that of a working map: a daily tool, read in a short morning session, so rows are compact (70px), figures are tabular, and the type stays in one family at modest sizes. Emphasis comes from weight and from the map colours, not from size jumps or decoration. The dark theme is the same sheet at night: same hues, lifted in lightness and muted in chroma, never glowing.

The world refuses the card-grid dashboard: KPI tiles, bordered or filled content panels, filled callouts and coloured side stripes. It refuses synthesized small caps (map lettering is real uppercase, tracked) and neon-on-dark.
keyCharacteristics: Warm-grey paper (light) or night-map charcoal (dark), ink text, four map colours with one job each.
Hairline rules (1px) separate everything; no content sits inside a card.
One content edge at 48px, a 360px title column, and a second edge where the scale bar and lifelines begin.
Time drawn, not listed: lifelines, a week scale bar, a today line and a movable seen mark.
Hanken Grotesk throughout; tracked uppercase map lettering for months and kommuner.
Motion is rare and meaningful: the seen mark sliding to today is the signature.

rules.name: The One Job Rule
rules.body: Each map colour means one thing: contour is time and map lettering, forest is new, lake is applied (and the interaction layer), rust is closing within 7 days. A colour that appears somewhere must mean its job there. Never use a map colour for decoration or for a second data meaning.

rules.name: The Never Only Colour Rule
rules.body: Every coloured state also has a word, a figure or a line style: "New", "Applied" and "Watching" as text, "3 days" beside a rust frist, today solid versus seen dashed, a legend under the sheet. Colour is never the only signal.

rules.name: The Night Map Rule
rules.body: Dark is the same sheet at night: the same four hues raised in lightness and lowered in chroma, on near-neutral charcoal. No neon, no glows, no pure black.

rules.name: The Map Lettering Rule
rules.body: Tracked uppercase (12px, 600, 0.1em) belongs to place and time names on the map: months and kommuner. It is never a section kicker, an eyebrow, a button style or a status label.

rules.name: The Real Caps Rule
rules.body: Map lettering is real uppercase with tracking. Never synthesize small caps (`font-variant: small-caps` on a family without them).

rules.name: The Two Edges Rule
rules.body: There is one content edge and one time edge. Content that is not drawn in time aligns to the content edge; anything drawn in time, or listed beside the title column, starts at the 360px time edge. Don't introduce a third.

rules.name: The Scale Bar Rule
rules.body: Time is read off one scale bar per sheet: alternating filled and hollow 4px week segments starting on Mondays (ink-secondary in light, ink-tertiary in dark), a 12px tabular date under each Monday (every other date hidden on narrow), and contour map-label month names above. Every lifeline on the sheet uses that same scale; never give rows their own scale.

rules.name: The Lifeline Rule
rules.body: A lifeline runs from the day an ad appeared to its frist. The past (appeared to today) is a 1px strong hairline, or 1.5px forest if new; it starts at a 7px dot (hollow ink-tertiary, or filled forest if new) or, if it began before the window, fades in over 40px with a "since" label. The future (today to frist) is 2px in the ad's one colour (contour open, lake applied, rust closing) and ends in a 2×12px tick with the frist and days left beside it (flipped above the line near the right edge). Closing beats applied: an applied ad closing within 7 days is rust.

rules.name: The Hairline Not Panel Rule
rules.body: Sections and rows are separated by 1px `rule` lines (top and bottom borders), never by enclosing boxes, filled panels or shadows.

dos: **Do** separate sections and rows with 1px `rule` hairlines and nothing else.
**Do** give each map colour exactly one job: contour for time and map lettering, forest for new, lake for applied and focus, rust for closing within 7 days.
**Do** pair every coloured state with a word, figure or line style, and carry the legend wherever lifelines are drawn.
**Do** align content to the one 48px edge and anything drawn in time to the 360px time edge.
**Do** set dates, counts and scale figures in tabular figures.
**Do** keep row actions revealed on hover and focus-within, and always visible when `hover: none`.
**Do** self-host Hanken Grotesk in the shipped app; it runs offline.
**Do** honour `prefers-reduced-motion` by removing the seen-mark slide and fades.
donts: **Don't** build cards, KPI tiles or bordered/filled content panels; the dashboard is one sheet.
**Don't** render needs-action or any alert as a filled callout or a box with a coloured side stripe; it is a sentence between hairlines.
**Don't** use tracked uppercase for kickers, eyebrows, buttons or status labels; it is map lettering for months and kommuner only.
**Don't** put a shadow on anything in the page flow; shadow is for floating layers only.
**Don't** use neon or glowing saturated hues on the dark theme; it is a night map of the same colours.
**Don't** use a map colour for decoration or a second meaning.
**Don't** load fonts from a CDN in the shipped app.
